faq.q: What is an AI YouTube Shorts ad?
faq.a: It is a tall creator-style Short. A hand can set the steamer on the shirt or give one reason to try it, with an [AI actor](/ai-video-generation/ai-actors) you can revoice. You pick the language, and you do not wait on a creator.

faq.q: Can a YouTube Shorts ad get people to watch longer?
faq.a: A steamer on a blue shirt is easier to stay with than a logo opening. If fewer people skip, you will see that in YouTube. We do not promise a longer watch.

faq.q: What does a YouTube Shorts ad cost?
faq.a: You pay credits for each Short. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: How real do the face and the voice look?
faq.a: The mouth meets the words, and the eyes stay on the steamer. The voice can sit in an accent you pick. If YouTube asks you to say the person is AI, say it.

faq.q: Can I change the script, the avatar, and the picture?
faq.a: Yes. Rewrite the line after you see the avatar, swap the hand on the steamer, and download the new Short.

faq.q: Will YouTube accept an AI Short as an ad?
faq.a: It can, if the steamer in the video is the steamer you ship and you say so when YouTube asks. We do not publish the ad for you. Read the disclosure rules on the day you post.

faq.q: Does a Short start from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. The product page can start the YouTube Shorts ad, and the steamer photo can start it too. If you also need the wide video that plays before another YouTube video, make that shape as its own file. Do not crop the Short and call it that wide video.

faq.q: Which frame should a Shorts ad use?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for Shorts. A 16:9 file is a separate wide job. Check [social media ad sizes](/guides/ad-sizes-by-platform) before you download, and keep the steamer clear of the player buttons.
